title: Trace the network route to a host
summary: Use traceroute to see the path your data takes to reach a website or server. It shows each 'hop' (router) and how long it takes to get there, helping you find where a connection is slow or broken.

steps.explain: Run traceroute with the hostname or IP address you want to reach. It will list each router (hop) and the time taken to reach it.

placeholders.name: HOST
placeholders.description: The domain name or IP address of the destination

steps.expect: A list of hops with IP addresses and response times.

alternatives.explain: Use -n to skip DNS lookups, making the output faster and showing only IP addresses.

placeholders.description: The domain name or IP address of the destination

alternatives.explain: Use -I to use ICMP packets instead of UDP, which some firewalls handle differently.
